days.title: Arrival in Prague
days.desc: Begin your journey in Prague, the “City of a Hundred Spires”, renowned for its medieval charm, stunning architecture and rich history. Unwind and prepare for a captivating stay. Overnight in Prague.
days.taste: A Czech Pilsner and svičková (marinated beef in cream sauce) at one of the pubs around Old Town Square — Prague's beer halls have been pouring since long before the city became a tourist draw.

days.title: Prague
days.desc: A guided tour reveals Prague Castle and the historic districts of Hradčany and Malá Strana, taking in St Vitus Cathedral, Golden Lane and the Old Royal Palace. The day closes with a leisurely cruise on the River Vltava, taking in the city's skyline from the water. Overnight in Prague.
days.experience: A 1-hour River Vltava cruise beneath Charles Bridge, with Prague Castle floodlit above the water as evening falls.
days.shopping: Parizska Street, running from Old Town Square toward the river, is Prague's boutique strip — alongside Bohemian crystal and garnet jewellery shops in the surrounding lanes.

days.title: Prague to Vienna
days.desc: Check out from Prague and continue on to Vienna, the “City of Music”, known for its imperial palaces, classical heritage and vibrant cultural scene. Overnight in Vienna.
days.taste: A slice of Sachertorte and a mélange (Vienna's take on a cappuccino) at one of the grand coffeehouses that have anchored Viennese social life since the 19th century.

days.title: Vienna
days.desc: A guided tour uncovers Vienna's imperial legacy, with a visit to the opulent Schönbrunn Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and its formal gardens. The tour continues through the elegant Innere Stadt, taking in the grandeur of Austria's capital. Overnight in Vienna.
days.experience: Schönbrunn Palace's formal gardens are free to walk even outside the palace tour hours — the Gloriette terrace above them gives one of Vienna's best skyline views.

days.title: Vienna to Budapest
days.desc: Check out from Vienna and continue to Budapest, the “Queen of the Danube”, known for its thermal baths, striking architecture and the historic Buda Castle. Overnight in Budapest.
days.taste: Goolyás (goulash soup) and a glass of Hungarian Tokaji or Egri Bikavér, best enjoyed in one of the bistros around Váci utca.

days.title: Budapest
days.desc: A guided city tour takes in Budapest's iconic landmarks — the Hungarian Parliament, Buda Castle, Matthias Church and the Fishermen's Bastion — before crossing into Pest to see the Central Market Hall, Europe's largest synagogue and Heroes' Square. Overnight in Budapest.
days.experience: Széchenyi Thermal Bath, one of Europe's largest spa complexes, is a short taxi ride from the centre and open into the evening — a properly Hungarian way to end the tour.

days.title: Depart Budapest
days.desc: Check out and bid farewell to Budapest with a private transfer from your hotel to the airport.

about.title: Best season
about.body: May–September for warm, long days on the river cruises; the Christmas markets (late Nov–Dec) give all three cities a festive alternative, with mulled wine on Old Town Square and Vienna's Rathausplatz.

about.title: Weather
about.body: Continental climate: warm summers around 20–28°C, cold winters that can drop below freezing, particularly in Prague and Budapest.

about.title: Currency & docs
about.body: Prague uses the Czech Koruna (CZK) and Budapest the Hungarian Forint (HUF) — neither is on the Euro; Vienna uses the Euro (€). All three are Schengen Area members, so no separate visa is needed for Schengen visa holders.

goodToKnow.title: Currency crossing borders
goodToKnow.body: Card payment is widely accepted in all three cities, but carry some local cash — CZK in Prague and HUF in Budapest — for markets, trams and smaller cafés; Euros are not usable outside Vienna.

goodToKnow.title: Train travel
goodToKnow.body: Seat reservations are included on the Prague–Vienna and Vienna–Budapest routes — keep tickets to hand for conductor checks.

goodToKnow.title: Photostops
goodToKnow.body: The Český Krumlov and Bratislava stops are brief photo and stretch breaks en route, not full guided visits — come with realistic expectations for time on the ground.

goodToKnow.title: What to pack
goodToKnow.body: Comfortable shoes for cobbled old towns; a warm layer even in summer evenings, as all three cities sit inland with cooler nights than their daytime highs suggest.

goodToKnow.title: Tipping
goodToKnow.body: 10% is customary in restaurants across all three cities, usually added directly when paying rather than left on the table.
